 was named this week among twenty-one global financial institutions that have agreed to form a joint venture intended to issue a dollar-denominated stablecoin, marking one of the most substantial collective moves yet by established banks into tokenised money. The group spans North America, Europe, East Asia, the Middle East and Africa, and the disclosure landed on the first trading day of as equity benchmarks slipped and bond yields climbed. The membership list reads like a roll call of large balance sheets. Alongside the firm sit Bank of America, Capital One, Citi, Fidelity, PNC, Scotiabank, TD Bank, Wells Fargo and WisdomTree from North America. European participants include Santander, BBVA, Commerzbank, Credit Agricole, Deutsche Bank, Lloyds, Rabobank and UBS. MUFG Bank, Standard Bank and an Abu Dhabi financial group round out the membership. Between them, the participants touch a very large share of global corporate and retail banking relationships. The plan, as described, is to establish a new company during the second half of this year, subject to closing conditions, and to launch a dollar-denominated stablecoin in the first half of next year. A euro-denominated offering is described as the next priority, with other major reserve currencies to follow after that. The token is intended to be backed one for one by reserves and issued on public blockchains, which distinguishes it from purely internal ledger systems that some institutions have built for their own clients. The stated use cases are wholesale, institutional and retail, spanning cross-border payments and digital asset settlement. In other words, the ambition is not a niche experiment but a general-purpose settlement instrument. The venture also has a lineage. Roughly a year earlier, a smaller group of about ten banks began exploring a reserve-backed form of digital money that would live on public chains. Membership has since more than doubled, and the effort has moved from exploration to a concrete plan to incorporate a company. That progression is itself part of the story, because it indicates the concept has cleared internal review at a large number of institutions with very different regulatory homes. Several forces are converging. Cross-border payments remain slow and costly relative to domestic transfers, particularly outside major corridors, because they rely on chains of correspondent relationships, each adding time, cost and reconciliation work. A token that settles instantly on a shared ledger removes several of those hops. Digital asset markets have also matured to the point where settlement of tokenised securities, funds and collateral requires a cash leg that lives on the same infrastructure. Without an on-chain dollar, the cash side of a tokenised trade still has to travel through legacy rails, which reintroduces the very delays that tokenisation was meant to remove. Then there is competitive defence. Privately issued dollar tokens already carry very large circulating balances, and the largest of them has become a significant holder of short-dated government paper. Payment flows that migrate onto those instruments bypass bank deposits, which is a structural concern for institutions whose funding depends on retaining customer balances. A consortium token allows banks to participate in that migration rather than watch it. Working together also spreads cost and reach. Building settlement infrastructure, reserve management, compliance screening and redemption mechanics is expensive, and a single-bank token is only as useful as that bank's client network. A shared instrument accepted by many institutions has a far better chance of achieving the network effects that make a settlement asset genuinely useful. Goldman Sachs has been active in digital asset infrastructure for several years, spanning tokenisation platforms, trading of digital asset derivatives for institutional clients, and research on how distributed ledgers might reshape market plumbing. The consortium sits comfortably alongside that work rather than replacing it. The firm's client base is heavily institutional, spanning asset managers, hedge funds, corporations, sovereign entities and financial sponsors. Those clients are precisely the users most likely to want on-chain settlement for tokenised funds, collateral movements and cross-border treasury operations. Participation in a widely accepted token gives the firm a way to serve that demand without building an isolated instrument that only its own clients could use. It also fits a broader pattern in how the firm has approached new markets: partnering where infrastructure is shared and competing where advice, execution and structuring add differentiated value. Settlement rails fall firmly into the first category. The venture has been framed explicitly around two rule sets. In the United States, the statute known as the GENIUS Act established a federal framework for payment stablecoins, covering reserve composition, redemption rights, disclosure and supervision. In Europe, the Markets in Crypto-Assets regulation set out authorisation requirements, reserve rules and conduct standards for token issuers operating across the bloc. Designing to both from the outset matters for an instrument intended to move across borders. A token that satisfies one regime but not the other would be limited to a single jurisdiction, which would undercut the cross-border case entirely. Building to the stricter of the two on each dimension is the practical route to a genuinely global instrument. Supervisory comfort is also a precondition for bank participation. Institutions of this size operate under capital, liquidity and conduct requirements that make unregulated experimentation impractical. The existence of clear statutory frameworks on both sides of the Atlantic is arguably the single biggest reason a group of this composition could form at all. The distinction that matters most is what sits behind the token. Existing dollar tokens are typically backed by portfolios of short-dated government securities and cash equivalents held by an issuer, with attestations published periodically. A bank consortium token backed one for one by reserves and issued under a statutory framework would carry a different supervisory wrapper, with redemption obligations and reserve rules embedded in law rather than in an issuer's own commitments. There is also a related but separate model in the market: the tokenised deposit. Rather than creating a new instrument, a deposit token represents an existing bank deposit on a distributed ledger, keeping the balance within the banking system and the claim against the issuing bank. At least one major American institution has pursued that route independently rather than joining the consortium, which means the settlement layer for institutional finance is being built along more than one design at once. Both approaches aim at the same practical outcome, namely cash that moves at the speed of tokenised assets. They differ in legal structure, in how balances interact with bank funding, and in how easily they move between institutions. For anyone tracking financial stocks through this period, the contest between those designs is one of the more consequential structural stories in the sector. Corporate treasury is the most obvious arena. Multinational companies manage cash across dozens of currencies and jurisdictions, and the friction of moving balances between them absorbs time and working capital. Instant settlement in a widely accepted token could compress that friction meaningfully, particularly for weekend and holiday transfers where traditional rails simply stop. Trade finance is another. Documentary credits, guarantees and supply chain finance all involve multiple parties in different jurisdictions, and payment timing is often the binding constraint. Settlement that clears in seconds rather than days changes the working capital arithmetic for both buyer and supplier. Securities settlement rounds out the picture. As tokenised funds, bonds and collateral instruments proliferate, the cash leg has to keep pace. Delivery against payment on a single ledger removes settlement exposure between counterparties, which is one of the oldest problems in market infrastructure. Beyond digital assets, the firm operates across advisory work, underwriting, markets execution, and asset and wealth management. Advisory and underwriting activity is tied closely to corporate confidence and financing conditions, both of which are sensitive to the same bond market moves that dominated the opening session of. The markets business tends to benefit from volatility, since client hedging and repositioning generate volume across rates, currencies, commodities and equities. The asset and wealth arm provides a steadier fee base, and the firm has continued to expand it, including an agreement announced in to acquire an exchange-traded fund specialist focused on options-based strategies. The firm also published a statement in on the results of the annual supervisory capital review, part of the recurring cycle that governs how much capital the largest institutions retain. That framework shapes capacity for balance sheet growth and distributions across the whole peer group. This material is general information only and is not advice. The sector enters the autumn with several crosscurrents. Long-dated Treasury yields have climbed toward multi-year highs, energy prices have surged on Middle East shipping disruption, and equity benchmarks opened on the back foot. Higher long rates change the arithmetic for lending, refinancing and securities portfolios simultaneously. At the same time, capital markets activity has been reasonably constructive, with issuance calendars filling and merger pipelines rebuilding. Firms weighted toward advisory and underwriting revenue depend on that activity continuing, and the autumn conference season typically brings updated commentary on how pipelines are shaping up. Technology spending is the other constant. Artificial intelligence tools are moving from pilots into production across document review, client servicing, code generation and surveillance. Distributed ledger work sits alongside that as a second technology track, and both absorb meaningful budget. The obvious challenge is incumbency. Privately issued dollar tokens already have deep liquidity, exchange integration and merchant acceptance across digital asset markets. A new entrant, however well capitalised, has to earn distribution rather than assume it. There is also the question of whether users want a bank-issued instrument. Digital asset natives prefer the tokens they already use, while corporate treasurers prefer instruments issued by institutions they already bank with. The answer probably varies by segment, which is why the venture has framed its scope across wholesale, institutional and retail markets rather than picking one. Coordination is a third challenge. Twenty-one institutions across many jurisdictions have to agree on governance, reserve management, technology choices and commercial terms. Consortium projects in financial infrastructure have a mixed record, and execution will matter as much as the concept. Reserve management is the first. A token backed one for one has to keep its backing in instruments that are liquid enough to meet redemptions at any hour, yet stable enough that the backing does not wobble when markets move. That points toward very short-dated government paper and central bank balances, which in turn means the venture becomes a meaningful participant in short-term funding markets. Round-the-clock operation is the second. Traditional settlement systems close, reconcile and reopen. A token that lives on a public chain does not, which means redemption, compliance screening and treasury operations have to run continuously across time zones. Staffing and automating that is a genuine operational undertaking rather than a technical footnote. Interoperability is the third. Tokens issued on one chain need routes to assets settled on another, and institutional users will not accept a settlement asset that strands them on a single network. Bridging arrangements, messaging standards and identity frameworks all have to be agreed before a token can serve as general infrastructure rather than a closed loop. Finally there is the question of how the instrument interacts with bank funding. If corporate balances migrate from deposits into a consortium token, the aggregate effect on bank funding depends on where the reserves sit. That accounting detail sounds technical, but it shapes how supervisors are likely to view the structure as balances grow. The near-term markers are procedural. Formation of the new company during the second half of this year is the first gate, followed by regulatory authorisations in the relevant jurisdictions. After that comes the technical question of which chains the token is issued on and how redemption operates across time zones. Commercial adoption is the deeper test. A settlement instrument becomes useful when enough counterparties accept it, which means the early corporate and institutional users will shape whether the network effect takes root. Watching which corridors and asset classes adopt it first will indicate where the friction was greatest. For a firm counted among the components of the S&P 500, the venture is one strand within a much larger franchise, but it is a strand that touches the plumbing of global finance rather than a single revenue line. That is what makes it worth following through the months ahead. title: BJP issues show-cause notice to Mandal GS in Tripura over anti-party activities - Tripuratimes
content: The Tripura unit of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) has issued a show-cause notice to Mahatwa Ranjan Chakma, general secretary of the 49-Chawmanu Mandal under Dhalai district, over allegations of engaging in anti-party activities and damaging the image of the organization. According to a press release issued by the party, allegations against Chakma of being involved in anti-party campaigning recently came to the attention of the state BJP president. The party alleged that such activities had not only tarnished the image of the BJP but had also created resentment among party workers. Chakma has also been accused of allegedly attempting to influence certain BJP functionaries to leave the party. In view of the allegations, and following the directions of the state BJP president, party state general secretary Bhagaban Chandra Das issued the show-cause notice to Chakma. The notice, according to the party, seeks an explanation from Chakma as part of efforts to maintain party discipline and ascertain the facts and circumstances behind the allegations. The BJP said the action was aimed at ensuring organizational discipline and protecting the party's image. 40, Akhaura Road, Agartala 799 001, Tripura, INDIA.

title: Vikings Sign OLB Kyle Van Noy, RB DeeJay Dallas to Practice Squad; Bring Back Brosmer & Bell - Minnesota Vikings
content:
EAGAN, Minn. — The Vikings on Wednesday signed two veterans, OLB Kyle Van Noy and RB DeeJay Dallas to their practice squad and brought back second-year QB Max Brosmer and rookie WR Dillon Bell. In corresponding moves, the team waived seventh-round rookie center Gavin Gerhardt, as well as two undrafted rookies — OL Tristan Leigh and OLB Cam'Ron Stewart — and guard Joshua Gray. Van Noy, 35, spent the past three seasons with Baltimore where he started 29 of 45 regular-season games and recorded 23.5 sacks and 39 hits on quarterbacks, including career highs of 12.5 and 21 in 2024. That production two years ago earned Van Noy his first Pro Bowl selection. He also is a two-time Super Bowl champion with the New England Patriots in 2016 and 2018. During that time, Van Noy played for New England linebackers coach and current Vikings Defensive Coordinator Brian Flores. Van Noy paced players in the 2018 postseason with three sacks. He notched a pair in the AFC Championship Game victory over Kansas City, and he had one in Super Bowl LIII, which was Flo's final game with New England before he accepted the head coaching job in Miami. Van Noy reunited with Flores on the Dolphins in 2020 and posted 69 tackles, 6.0 sacks and six passes defended. View photos of the Vikings 53-man roster as of Aug. 31, 2026. In 12 NFL seasons, Van Noy has tallied 561 tackles, including 74 for losses, 57 sacks, 39 passes defended, 14 forced fumbles, four interceptions and three defensive touchdowns. He entered the league in 2014 as a second-round pick by Detroit out of BYU where he had 25 sacks in 52 contests. The 6-foot-3, 255-pound Van Noy has suited up for five franchises in total: Detroit (2014-16); New England (2016-19, 2021); Miami (2020); the Los Angeles Chargers (2022); and Baltimore (2023-25). Van Noy joins a Vikings OLB room that consists of Andrew Van Ginkel, Dallas Turner, Bo Richter and Chaz Chambliss on the 53-man roster. Second-year defender Tyler Batty was placed on season-ending Injured Reserve on Sunday. Dallas, 27, was a fourth-round draft pick by Seattle in 2020 out of Miami and is reuniting with General Manager Nolan Teasley after spending 2025 with Carolina and Jacksonville. He appeared in 61 games for the Seahawks from 2020-23 and 17 for Arizona in 2024 prior to splitting time with the Panthers and Jaguars. In 84 career games, Dallas has rushed 124 times for 538 yards and four touchdowns. He also has caught 64 passes for 407 yards and two scores and returned 89 kickoffs for an average of 25.3 yards and one touchdown. Brosmer and Bell were with Minnesota throughout the offseason and training camp. Brosmer went 1-1 in two starts last season. Bell was added after the 2026 NFL Draft out of Georgia and contributed in the run and pass games during the preseason. title: Stream Karol G’s “No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto” featuring Drake, Bruno Mars and more - Dailyfly News
content: Grammy-winning Colombian recording artist Karol G has officially released her sixth full-length studio project, No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto. The the 14-track collection stands out for its star-studded guest list, headlined by long-awaited collaborations with Drake on the track “Ahí” and Bruno Mars on the R&B-infused ballad “Still“. Additional features across the record include Cigarettes After Sex frontman Greg Gonzalez on “Después de Ti,” alongside rising Spanish vocalists Judeline and Rusowsky on “Bby Wow”. Moving away from the energetic, tropical rhythms that defined her 2025 release Tropicoqueta, the new material explores vulnerability, emotional recovery, and nostalgia. During a recent concert at Toronto’s Rogers Stadium where she initially announced the project, the performer explained that the album “opens a door for my fans to a more intimate Carolina.” Inspiration for the record began taking shape during solo trips through Hawaii, where the singer reflected on the isolation that can accompany fame. Production was handled primarily in low-lit studio sessions featuring frequent collaborator Ovy on the Drums alongside producers Tainy, Cashmere Cat, and KEITYN. The release coincides directly with the ongoing North American leg of Karol’s Viajando Por El Mundo Tropitour, following record-breaking stadium performances. Following scheduled stops in Las Vegas, the tour is slated to cross North America, Mexico, South America, and Europe through mid-2027. title: GS Caltex Tightens Defense, Eyes Consecutive Title - 조선일보
content: Defending champions diversify attacks, add Tanacha to reduce Silva's burden after historic win [Cheongpyeong=Sports Chosun Kim Young-rok Reporter] "Through an unexpected championship that no one anticipated, the players have grown significantly. The team has become more solid overall." The 'underdog' achieved a historic championship. Now, they are aiming for a second consecutive title. GS Caltex defied all expectations in the 2025-2026 season, securing third place in the regular season. In the postseason, they achieved six consecutive wins against Heungkuk Life, Hyundai Engineering & Construction, and Korea Expressway Corporation, clinching the championship trophy. This marked the team's first title in six years since the 2020-2021 season. At Cheongpyeong GS Caltex, head coach Lee Young-Taek, discussing preparations for the new season, said, "Although we won the championship, we aimed to bring changes to the team's strength. With Tanacha's addition, we could reduce Silva's burden, and it was impressive to see our players grow even further," expressing pride. "He floated in the air for two days after winning. Now that the new season is approaching, I feel the surrounding expectations. The pressure has definitely increased," he sighed. However, he emphasized, "It became an opportunity to understand how to win championships. The team atmosphere, unity, and focus were excellent. The players themselves know what kind of volleyball they should play, and my task as a coach is to bring that out on the court." Ultimately, GS Caltex's challenge is to reduce reliance on 'queen' Gyselle Silva's attacks. Even after last season's victory, they couldn't avoid criticism like 'ultimately a one-woman Silva championship' and 'Gyselle Silva Caltex.' Silva recorded 1,005 points, 1,008 points, and 1,083 points over three years in Korea, achieving the remarkable feat of scoring over 1,000 points for three consecutive years. However, Silva, born in 1991, is at an age where each year brings significant change. Coach Lee Young-Taek stated, "Scoring over 1,000 points is proof of Silva's consistent outstanding performance, so it's not bad. Still, I want to lessen Silva's attacking burden. This year, we have high expectations for the Asian quota player Tanacha. We aim to demonstrate more diverse attack distribution and ideal volleyball this year." After the championship, the team had a quiet off-season. Compared to the previous season, only the Asian quota player changed from Reina Tokoku to Tanacha Sooksom. Tanacha is in her fourth season in Korea. She is praised for her exceptional stamina and attacking skills and has quickly adapted to GS Caltex. Additionally, the team recruited two Japanese coaches: Kawamura Shinji and Ishii Sugurou. Coach Kawamura has been acquainted with Lee Young-Taek since his playing days and has experience as a coach in the Japanese league. Coach Sugurou is responsible for guiding GS Caltex's young setters: Kim Ji-won, Lee Yoon-shin, and Choi Yoon-young. If Silva and Tanacha are fixed, the remaining wing position is for one outside hitter. Fierce competition is expected among Yoo Seo-yeon, Kwon Min-ji, Lee Ju-a, Kim Ju-hyang, and Kim Mi-yeon. The head coach emphasized, "These are players with strong individuality. There will be timing when bold changes are needed during games. Other players must support Silva well. Now is the time for competition. I hope they show the roles they can play." For middle blockers, Oh Se-yeon has solidified her position, leaving one remaining spot contested between Choi Ga-eun and Choi Yu-rim. Coach Lee Young-Taek explained, "Oh Se-yeon has established herself, and her desire to perform better and win again is evident. Last season, we focused on Choi Yu-rim's growth because Choi Ga-eun was injured, but Choi Ga-eun also performed well in the latter half, with the advantage of abundant energy. We will keep both players competing until the day before the opening match." When Oh Se-yeon's name came up, Yoo Seo-yeon raised her voice: "During the championship match, I saw Seo-yeon overcoming difficulties and striving, and I thought she had become a completely different player. Her mindset had changed," she smiled brightly. The libero position is also solid with Han Soo-jin and Yoo Ga-ram, and Kim Hyo-im has significantly improved after recently returning from the national team. GS Caltex's signature net defense is expected to remain formidable this season. GS Caltex aims to become a 'consistently strong team' that continuously advances to the spring playoffs without being complacent about their past victory. When asked to predict this season's structure, the head coach's tone turned serious. He said, "Lightheartedly, I think Hyundai Engineering & Construction will continue to perform well. Industrial Bank of Korea (IBK) struggled early last season but showed strong form in the latter half. The rest will be a mix. This season will likely see many coaches with more gray hair," he laughed. "Ultimately, injury management is most important. Every team has a clear gap between starters and substitutes." "Last season's media day, we stated our goal was over 20 wins and 60 points. We achieved 19 wins and 57 points. I believe the playoff qualification is around 60 points. Once we reach the playoffs, we have Silva. We will book a hotel for the championship match in advance. We will do our best to avoid a 'no-show.'" title: GS Retail Collects 1,000 Used Electronics in Recycling Drive - Seoul Economic Daily
content: GS Retail (007070) said on the 2nd that it held an event to collect discarded electronic products at GS Tower in Seoul's Gangnam district. Heo Seo-hong, chief executive of GS Retail, joined the event along with GS25 store operators, GS Retail employees and staff from GS affiliates. The event was part of the "Our Neighborhood Resource Circulation Campaign," run with E-Circulation Governance, a recycling agency under the Ministry of Environment. It was held ahead of Resource Circulation Day on the 6th of this month. Employees brought in their own discarded electronics for collection. Participants received gifts including Seoul Milk desserts and coffee from GS25. About 700 people took part, and more than 1,000 used electronic products were collected. The collected items will be recycled through E-Circulation Governance. "This campaign was a meaningful occasion for our employees to put the value of resource circulation into practice in their daily lives," said Park Kyung-rang, head of GS Retail's ESG team. "We will continue to expand a range of resource circulation activities that customers and employees can join together, based on GS25 and GS The Fresh stores nationwide." title: GS Retail wraps up e-waste recycling campaign with CEO, staff participation - 헤럴드경제
content: GS Retail successfully concluded a used electronics collection event Wednesday morning at GS Tower in Gangnam-gu, Seoul. The event was held as part of the "Our Neighborhood Resource Circulation Campaign," organized ahead of Resource Circulation Day on Sunday in partnership with E-Circulation Governance, a recycling agency under the Ministry of Climate, Environment and Energy. GS Retail CEO Heo Seo-hong, GS25 store owners, and employees from GS Retail and its affiliates brought in their own discarded electronics to take part in the collection drive. Participants received Seoul Milk desserts and coffee from GS25. More than 700 people took part in the event, with over 1,000 used electronic items collected. The items will be processed for resource recycling through E-Circulation Governance. GS Retail plans to expand resource circulation activities for both employees and customers, drawing on its network of more than 18,600 stores nationwide under GS25 and GS The Fresh. Park Gyeong-rang, head of GS Retail's ESG division, said the event was "a meaningful occasion for employees to put the value of resource circulation into practice in their daily lives," adding that the company would "continue to expand a wide range of resource circulation activities going forward."

title: PIPC narrows GS Retail penalty by excluding franchise supply revenue - CHOSUNBIZ - Chosunbiz
content: Penalty hinges on excluding B2B franchise sales and supermarket revenue after credential-stuffing breach at GS Shop and GS25 In calculating the 12.836 billion won penalty surcharge for a personal data leak imposed on the 31st on GS Retail(25,500 won ▼ 450 -1.73%), the Personal Information Protection Commission excluded franchise supply sales—more than 70% of the company's total revenue—from the benchmark used to compute the surcharge. The move contrasts with the record 624.681 billion won imposed on Coupang three months earlier, confirming that the severity of sanctions can vary widely depending on a retailer's revenue structure. The action stems from an incident in which, from June 2024 to Feb. this year, hackers launched a brute-force login attack on the GS SHOP and GS25 websites operated by GS Retail, leaking the names, contact information, and addresses of 1,661,53 members. According to the industry on the 2nd, the Personal Information Protection Commission viewed about 8 trillion won of GS Retail's roughly 11.5 trillion won average revenue over the past three fiscal years—sales recorded when headquarters supplies goods to franchisees—as unrelated to the violations and excluded it. It judged the revenue to be business-to-business (B2B) transactions with no direct link to the data leak. As a result, the sales figure used as the basis for calculating the penalty surcharge fell to the 2 trillion won range. Under the Personal Information Protection Act, a penalty surcharge is calculated based on total revenue minus revenue unrelated to the violations and cannot exceed 3% of total revenue. The business operator must directly prove the unrelated revenue. GS Retail's business report shows revenue of 11.0803 trillion won in 2023, 11.5794 trillion won in 2024, and 11.9574 trillion won in 2025. The final sticking point was reportedly whether to include sales from the GS The Fresh supermarket chain. GS Retail uses a unified database (DB) across home shopping, convenience stores, and supermarkets, but this attack occurred only at GS SHOP and GS25. Because the DB is shared, some argued supermarket sales should be included, while others countered that a division not actually attacked could not be counted; in the end, supermarket sales were excluded from the benchmark. The attack method also appears to have influenced the outcome. In this incident, hackers used "credential stuffing," repeatedly trying IDs and passwords obtained externally. Because websites with login procedures were targeted, only GS SHOP and GS25 were breached. The commission's internal view was that if the unified DB server itself had been directly attacked, total revenue including supermarkets could have been counted. For that reason, during deliberations, members reportedly raised the view that, going forward, the calculation benchmark could vary depending on the revenue recognition structure, the attack vector, and the scope and types of data leaked. Even if the same company suffers a repeat incident of the same type, there is no guarantee franchise supply sales would be excluded again. The retail industry says the outcome stands in sharp contrast to the Coupang case three months earlier. In June, the Personal Information Protection Commission imposed a total penalty surcharge of 624.681 billion won on Coupang, including 423.575 billion won related to the leak and 201.106 billion won related to infringements such as the unauthorized collection of activity records from other companies' online services. At the time, the Personal Information Protection Commission used the revenue of Coupang's e-commerce service, where the incident occurred, as the benchmark for the surcharge and excluded only divisions separately notified as distinct services, such as Coupang Eats and Coupang Play. During deliberations, Coupang argued that, because it directly purchases goods from manufacturing small and midsize businesses, the entire transaction amount was overstated as its revenue, but the claim was ultimately not accepted. Coupang has said it will file an administrative lawsuit to contest the action. We use cookies to enhance your experience and analyze traffic. title: Meet U of G’s First Schulich Leaders - U of G News
content: Canada’s largest undergraduate STEM scholarships support entrepreneurial-minded students Learning how to put AI to use for the greater good and helping Canadian farmers with food sustainability are the goals of two Schulich Leaders who will begin their journeys at the University of Guelph this fall. Aryan Thakur will pursue computer engineering and Matteo Volpini will study agriculture with the support of Schulich Leader Scholarships, Canada’s most prestigious STEM scholarship program. Schulich Leader Scholarships provide $100,000 for a science, technology or math degree, or $120,000 for an engineering degree, for entrepreneurial-minded students. U of G is proud to be part of the prestigious scholarship program as it’s a testament to the University’s ability to attract some of Canada’s most competitive STEM students who aspire to careers in tech, engineering and applied research. “As we celebrate 15 years of Schulich Leaders, we are proud to have supported more than 1,000 exceptional Canadian students pursuing STEM degrees at our country’s top universities,” says Judy Schulich, president, The Schulich Foundation. “Schulich Leader Scholarships help attract and retain outstanding talent, empowering the next generation of innovators and entrepreneurs. By supporting their ambition and creating the conditions for them to succeed, we can ensure their innovations drive Canada’s future prosperity.” A Schulich Leader Scholarship is life changing, says Aryan Thakur, whose interest in artificial intelligence and machine learning drew him to U of G’s Computer Engineering program in the College of Engineering. As part of a generation who grew up alongside technology, Thakur knew early on he wanted to be part of an industry revolutionizing the world. “AI and machine learning are going to provide a lot of opportunity,” he says, “and I want to align myself with that.” Eager to launch his own start-up, Thakur says his program’s co-op stream is the kind of experiential learning that will build a foundation for him, from which to grow his own ideas. He knows there is work to do in the field. AI is not yet functioning at 100%, and so he is dedicated to being part of improving it, ultimately putting it to use for good. “I want to help people,” he says, “using technology to have a meaningful impact.” Being a Schulich Leader is about more than just financial support, he says. “The ability to network with fellow Scholars really does help with job opportunities or even just aligning with others going through the same life transition.” It was while growing up on a small hobby farm learning tree pruning and how to pick cherries and peaches and apples that Matteo Volpini learned the kind of devastation disease can bring to plants and the crops of farmers. The years his family lost nearly 200 trees to disease, pests and the environment, he started researching where he could study plant science and food sustainability. What he found was the Bachelor of Science in Agriculture program at the Ontario Agricultural College. “I’m excited to learn more about gene-editing technology, gain more plant knowledge and learn how disease affects plants, how pesticides and fungicides can help prevent these things,” he says. His goals don’t end there. “I’d like to start a business dedicated to global food sustainability that supports Canadian farmers by developing resilient crop varieties that can better withstand environmental stressors like pests, disease and unpredictable weather.” As a Schulich Leader, he joins a community of STEM students with similar interests across a broad spectrum of disciplines. “It’s such a great resource to have,” he says. “There are so many opportunities to learn from each other or to collaborate.” Recognizing the increasing importance and impact that STEM disciplines have on the prosperity of future generations, businessman and philanthropist Seymour Schulich established this $200 million scholarship fund in 2012 to encourage our best and brightest students to become Schulich Leader Scholars: the next generation of entrepreneurial-minded, technology innovators. Through The Schulich Foundation and United Jewish Appeal, these prestigious entrance scholarships are awarded to 100 high school graduates enrolling in a science, technology, engineering or mathematics (STEM) undergraduate program at 20 partner universities in Canada. Every high school in Canada can submit one Schulich Leader Nominee per academic year based entrepreneurial leadership and financial need.

title: GS Retail fined $9.3M following customer data breach - Mobility Plaza
content: South Korea’s privacy regulator imposed a 12.8 billion-won fine after a cyberattack exposed the personal information of more than 1.66 million GS SHOP and GS25 customers. GS Retail has been fined 12.8 billion won (approximately $9.3 million) by South Korea’s Personal Information Protection Commission (PIPC) following a data breach that affected more than 1.66 million customers across its GS SHOP and GS25 businesses. According to the regulator, an unidentified hacker gained access to customer accounts between 2024 and 2025 by using previously obtained user IDs and passwords to repeatedly attempt logins until successfully bypassing the company’s authentication systems. The incident compromised the personal information of around 1.58 million GS SHOP users and 79,128 GS25 customers. Exposed data included names, gender, dates of birth, phone numbers, home addresses and email addresses, as reported by The Korea Times. The PIPC said GS Retail failed to detect warning signs of suspicious activity, including a sudden increase in login attempts and authentication failures originating from the same IP addresses within a short period. As a result, the unauthorized access continued for an extended time without being identified. The regulator also found that the company did not have a dedicated privacy protection office in place at the time of the breach. In response, the PIPC ordered GS Retail to implement stronger safeguards, including security measures capable of identifying abnormal connections and access patterns. The company was also instructed to appoint dedicated personnel responsible for privacy protection.

title: GS E&C opens large Mokdong Yoonseul Xi officetel, tests Korea luxury demand - CHOSUNBIZ - Chosunbiz
content: Balconies, duplex spa and sky community headline GS E&C's supersized officetel as pricing reveal looms On the morning of the 1st, as soon as I stepped into the GS Engineering & Construction 'Mok-dong Yoonseul Xi' sample home in Mok-dong, Yangcheon-gu, Seoul, a massive media wall covering the entire wall first caught the eye. The screen showed countless exterior panels moving with the wind, reflecting light and creating ripples. It expressed the complex's name, "Yoonseul," through the building's exterior. Yoonseul is a pure Korean word meaning the sparkling appearance of sunlight or moonlight glinting on waves. Going up to the second floor, a model of a complex with six underground floors and up to 48 above-ground floors across three buildings appeared. Judging by the model alone, it was far from a typical officetel. The configuration with a tower rising to 48 floors, low-rise retail, and high-rise community facilities was closer to a luxury residential-commercial apartment complex. But Mok-dong Yoonseul Xi is an officetel, not an apartment. It consists of a total of 651 units with exclusive areas ranging from 114 to 203 square meters. Even the smallest unit is 114 square meters of exclusive area. GS Engineering & Construction named this type of product a "Hypert," meaning it combines an apartment's spatial layout with services of a high-end residential product. It is essentially a more upscale version of the large "apartment-style officetel" commonly discussed in the real estate market. Entering the 114-square-meter B unit prepared on the third floor revealed what features this complex chose to narrow the gap with apartments. In officetels, the ratio of exclusive area within the supply area is generally lower than in apartments, which can make interiors feel tighter. Mok-dong Yoonseul Xi added balconies to every unit to offset this drawback. The 114-square-meter B unit has five balconies. The balconies consolidation to the living room and bedrooms were fitted out as a study, a study room, and relaxation spaces. A pantry, multi-storage units, and built-in closets were also installed throughout. A sales representative said, "About 5 pyeong of balcony space is added to roughly 35 pyeong of exclusive area," and explained, "The space you can actually use is about 40 pyeong." In the 203-square-meter unit, the high ceiling was the first thing that stood out when entering the foyer. Climbing the interior stairs leads to an outdoor terrace, and the terrace in the sample home features a spa tub. It is designed so residents can enjoy a bath in the exterior space of a high-rise building in the city. The duplex-type product will be placed on the 45th to 48th floors. They also focused on upgrading the community facilities. On the first to third basement floors, the about 3,000-pyeong membership wellness club 'Concord Club by Josun,' directly entrusted to and operated by Josun Hotels & Resorts, will open. On the 47th floor, they placed the sky community 'Club Cloud.' After touring the flashy sample home, the question that ultimately remains is price. The market speculated that the presale price of Mok-dong Yoonseul Xi could approach 1 billion won per 3.3 square meters based on exclusive area. The 114-square-meter unit is about 34.5 pyeong, so applying that price would put the simple calculated presale price over 3.4 billion won. A sales representative on this day drew a line, saying, "It is not 1 billion won per 3.3 square meters based on exclusive area." Specific presale prices are set to be released after presale approval and the recruitment notice on the 2nd. It appears a pricing method will be applied with relatively lower prices for the lower floors and higher prices for the upper floors. The sample home will officially open on the 3rd. GS Engineering & Construction cited as a basis for price competitiveness the fact that nearby apartments, such as Mok-dong New Town Complex 7, which is in its 40th year since completion, and Hyundai Hyperion, which is over 20 years old, are changing hands in the 3-billion-won range. A sales representative said, "Comparing older apartments with newly built products, we judge the price to be within the range the area can accept." The bar for subscriptions and loans is lower than for apartments. Anyone 19 or older can apply regardless of whether they have a subscription savings account, own dwellings, or where they live. Winners are selected by lottery, not by points. For officetel mortgage loans, the non-dwelling mortgage LTV can be applied up to a maximum of 70%. However, the actual loan amount varies depending on the collateral appraisal value, the debt service ratio (DSR), and existing liability. Mok-dong Yoonseul Xi will rise on the former KT site at 924 Mok-dong, Yangcheon-gu. It is about a 10-minute walk from Omokgyo Station on Subway Line 5. The developer said that due to overcrowding at Mogun Elementary School, resident children are expected to be assigned to Seojeong Elementary School. title: GS Retail fined $9.4mn over personal data leak - 매일경제
content: GS Retail Co., a South Korean retail giant that operates GS25 convenience stores, has been fined 12.8 billion won ($9.35 million) and ordered to pay an administrative penalty of 3 million won for a personal data breach affecting about 1.66 million members after failing to implement adequate security measures, including access controls. The Personal Information Protection Commission (PIPC), the country’s privacy watchdog, said on Monday that it approved the sanctions at its 17th plenary meeting on August 26. The measures include the fine and administrative penalty, a corrective order, and a requirement for GS Retail to publish the results on its website. According to the PIPC’s investigation, an unidentified hacker carried out credential-stuffing attacks against the GS SHOP home shopping website from June 21, 2024, to February 13, 2025, and against the GS25 convenience store website from December 26, 2024, to January 4, 2025. Credential stuffing is a type of cyberattack in which attackers repeatedly attempt to log in using usernames and passwords obtained through other channels. “Since the incident, we have conducted a comprehensive review of our security management system and strengthened our information security,” GS Retail said. “We have also established an Information Security Countermeasures Committee involving external experts and are continuing our efforts to prevent a recurrence.” Samsung Electronics, SK hynix fall on renewed Middle East te.. The exterior design of the lower levels particularly caught the eye, having panels on the façade that move organically with the wind and the angle of light through collaboration with world-renowned kinetic artist Ned Kahn. The design expresses 'Yunsul', a Korean word meaning 'the shimmering ripples of sunlight or moonlight on the water', on the building's façade. On the 1st, the model house of "Mokdong Yoonsul Xi" was set up near the former KT Mokdong site in Yangcheon-gu, Seoul. A precise large-scale complex model consisting of 3 buildings with up to 48 floors has been installed. GS Construction The luxurious community facilities within the complex were also noteworthy. On basement levels B1 to B3, a 9,900-square-meter membership wellness club called 'Concord Club by Josun', operated by Josun Hotel & Resort, will be located. Although situated underground, the space utilizes a 'sunken' architectural design to allow for natural lighting. The club will include amenities such as an indoor swimming pool, fitness center, golf practice range, and sauna. In addition, the sky community 'Club Cloud', which allows residents to enjoy dining, parties, work, and cultural activities all in one place while taking in the view, will be established on the 47th and top floor of Building 102. There will be purpose-specific spaces such as a wine reserve, cafeteria, guest house, and sound chamber. On the third floor of the model housing, various residential spaces were on display, with three unit types available: 114㎡B, 115㎡A, and the duplex-style 203㎡AD. The 114㎡B unit maximized lighting and ventilation with a living room open on both sides of the building. It features five balconies, each designed for different uses, attracting attention. Targeted for a three-person household of a couple in their 30s and a preschool-aged child, the interior combines white tones with wood and fabric. Two of the balconies connected to the master bedroom are designated as a relaxation zone and a home gym, with one side equipped with a bench and rug, and the other with a training monitor mounted on the wall. The balcony connected to the living room extends the living space, and the balcony next to the kitchen serves as a study-type dining area with a wall-length bookshelf. The child’s room balcony is set as a focused study area. The design treats the balconies as full rooms rather than just service areas. The 115㎡A unit emphasizes a calm atmosphere by pairing black and white tones with wood and stone accents, targeting four-person households of couples in their early 40s with middle and elementary school children, and focusing on storage and children's spaces. (BAC) surged to annual highs after the banks posted stellar second-quarter earnings results that beat market expectations. GS stock led the climb among banking stocks, surging more than 9% after its record Q2 results triggered a buy-in. JPM stock rose 2.5% after its results surged past Wall Street expectations, while BAC stock also soared nearly 2% to a record high. GS stock climbed to a record high of $1,143.84 on Tuesday after the company reported record Q2 results that tore past analysts’ expectations. Goldman Sachs posted quarterly revenue of $20.98 billion, significantly higher than Wall Street's $16.4 billion estimate, according to Koyfin data. The investment bank also reported earnings of $15.91 per share, ahead of the $14.40 consensus estimate, while net income reached a record $6.32 billion for the quarter. The strong results were fueled by robust performance in investment banking, equities trading, and asset management, as companies continued to tap capital markets and pursue AI-related financing and strategic deals. "There's a lot of capital out there," CEO David Solomon said in an interview with CNBC on Tuesday. "I'm not concerned about the ability for the capital to be available for things that make sense." Beck called SpaceX a “friendly rival” and said space companies often compete for one contract before working together on another: “You can be competing tooth and tail for a particular contract” and later team up to deliver it, he said. Rocket Lab can also benefit when rivals win as it supplies components such as reaction wheels, star trackers and solar panels.” “We can go head to head with a traditional space prime and then lose,” Beck said. “And then the next day, there’s a purchase order.” Beck called Rocket Lab an end-to-end space company spanning satellites, launch and services from orbit: “We build satellites, we launch them on our rockets and we provide services from space,” he said. Could be an inflection point if positive.” For updates and corrections, email newsroom[at]stocktwits[dot]com. Comments posted here will also appear on symbol pages. General Fusion Group Ltd. (GFUZ) made history on Monday, becoming the first pure-play nuclear fusion energy company to trade on a major public stock exchange. In an exclusive interview with Stocktwits, CEO Greg Twinney argued that fusion is not just a cleaner alternative to fission but is a fundamentally larger market opportunity. GFUZ stock surged 21% on its debut, added over 25% on Tuesday, and was trading about 2.5% lower in the overnight session. The Vancouver-based company, backed by Amazon founder Jeff Bezos, among others, went public through a SPAC merger with Spring Valley Acquisition Corp. III, which provided General Fusion with approximately $150 million in cash. Earlier, Twinney told the Wall Street Journal that the funding is sufficient to meet the scientific milestones required by its demonstration machine. The listing arrives at a pivotal moment. Surging electricity demand driven by the AI boom, the global spread of electrification, and the energy appetite of large-scale computing has renewed urgency around new sources of firm, clean power. Fusion has attracted growing investment and government attention as a potential long-term answer. According to the Financial Times, the number of private fusion companies has more than doubled over the past five years, intensifying competition at a time when the technology is still roughly a decade from commercialization. General Fusion is targeting its first commercial plant around 2035. Twinney's bull case for fusion starts with what it doesn't produce. Unlike fission, fusion does not generate long-lived radioactive waste, does not use fuels that could be weaponized, and carries no risk of a meltdown. "Fusion is just inherently safe. We're not needing to engineer safety into it in the same way that you need to with fission," he told Stocktwits. "When fusion fails, it kind of just fails safely and there's not really any fallout from that." That safety profile has a direct commercial implication: regulators around the world are moving to govern fusion "in a much lighter way" than conventional nuclear, Twinney said, which he believes creates the potential to site fusion plants closer to population centers and industrial demand. That's a significant advantage over fission, which requires remote, heavily secured facilities. "We get all the benefits that fission can provide without the downsides," he said. There's another significant advantage. Fusion reactors primarily use deuterium, which can be extracted from seawater and is "massively abundant." The other component, tritium, is rarer in nature but can be bred through the interaction of a neutron and lithium. Fission, by contrast, relies on uranium and other finite sources. "The overall market size because of the safety profile and the abundance of fuel in fusion is much bigger than fission," Twinney said. While advanced nuclear companies such as Oklo Inc. (OKLO) and NuScale Power Corp. (SMR) are often thought of as being closer to commercialization than fusion technology, Twinney said that the gap may not be as large as investors assume. While the road to commercialization for fusion technology has its challenges, including achieving reactor durability, tritium fuel breeding, economic viability, and the ability to efficiently extract and convert fusion energy into electricity, he argues small modular reactor (SMR) timelines also struggle with regulatory hurdles that can make timelines less predictable than they appear today. "I know that the timelines for SMRs, which can be very unpredictable due to regulations and those types of things, [are] probably not that different," he said. According to Twinney, the combination of abundant fuel supplies and a lighter regulatory framework could ultimately enable fusion to scale faster than conventional nuclear technologies once commercial viability has been demonstrated. However, Twinney does not view fusion and fission as mutually exclusive technologies. "They will be complementing each other," he said. "And I think that fusion kind of rounds out the nuclear circle if you think about it that way," he added. When asked about criticism from former Commonwealth Fusion Systems CTO Dan Brunner, who, in a recent interview with the Financial Times, said General Fusion's commercialization timeline was "very hard to believe," Twinney said the company’s timelines were based on real experimental results from its Lawson Machine 26. The machine is designed to demonstrate that plasma can be heated through mechanical compression rather than superconducting magnets or high-powered lasers, he said, adding that the company's early results validated the operating principles behind its MTF approach that are “not based on fiction or papers being written.” The timelines “are based on our real results from machines that we have built and operated and then eventually written papers on. But those are real results papers, not theoretical papers,” he said. Twinney also emphasized that General Fusion's approach could offer a cost advantage over many competing technologies. While many other fusion developers rely on expensive superconducting magnets, high-powered lasers, or advanced materials that have yet to be proven at commercial scale, General Fusion's Magnetized Target Fusion (MTF) system uses mechanical compression and a liquid-lithium wall that can protect reactor components from neutron damage, help with breeding tritium fuel, and absorbing fusion energy as heat that can be converted into electricity using conventional steam turbines. In an earlier interview with Stocktwits, Chief Strategy Officer Megan Wilson had also pointed to the economic advantages of MTF, which eliminate the need for expensive magnets, targets, lasers, or exotic, not-yet-invented materials. The technology also eliminates the need for frequent replacement of components damaged by neutron exposure, she had said. “Our plants are designed to be cost-competitive compared to coal, steam, and natural gas,” she had said then. “They are expected to deliver four times as much energy per unit of fuel as fission, without long-lived radioactive waste, positioning them as the superior nuclear technology for sustainable growth.” By avoiding costly magnets and lasers and using existing industrial technologies, Twinney said he believes General Fusion has a clearer path to building an economically viable power plant, as the company’s design has from the beginning aimed to avoid the major barriers to commercializing fusion. "What we are trying to do at General Fusion, and our power plant design from the beginning, has been we want to avoid the major barriers to commercializing fusion. Not just demonstrate a bunch of fusion, but actually avoid the barriers to commercializing it," he said. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around GFUZ stock is ‘bullish’ amid ‘high’ message volumes. title: Heungkuk sees GS Holdings boost profits as key units power South Korea gains - CHOSUNBIZ - Chosunbiz
content: Heungkuk securities said on the 1st that GS Holdings(078930), backed by operating profit growth at key subsidiaries, is expected to post solid results this year. It maintained a "Buy" investment rating and raised the target price to 170,000 won. GS Holdings' previous closing price was 127,100 won. For GS Holdings' third-quarter results this year on a consolidation basis, revenue is forecast at 7.7 trillion won and operating profit at 1.5 trillion won. Those would be up 18.8% and 67.1%, respectively, from a year earlier, and the company is expected to continue delivering solid operating results following the previous quarter. Some subsidiaries are showing weakness, but key subsidiaries GS Energy and GS Caltex are expected to continue generating solid operating profit, and GS Retail's results are also projected to keep growing. This year's full-year results on a consolidation basis were slightly revised up to revenue of 29.7 trillion won, up 17.9% from a year earlier, and operating profit of 5.7 trillion won, up 94.1%. Park Jong-ryeol of Heungkuk securities said, "Unlike last year, GS Caltex and GS Energy's operating performance this year will likely remain steady," adding, "That's because GS Energy's power and district energy and resource development are generating stable profit, and GS Caltex's refining margins for refining and lubricants are also likely to stay firm." The analysis was that this is because supply-demand instability will continue due to geopolitical risks and operating disruptions in the region. Park also said, "Most subsidiaries, including GS Retail, GS P&L and GS Global, are expected to see gradual improvement in results." In addition, GS Group plans to build a 2.4 GW mega-scale AI data center campus in Gangwon Province with a total investment of 30 trillion won. Park explained, "GS Power, GS EPS and GS E&R have know-how in supplying large volumes of stable electricity for AI data centers, and GS Engineering & Construction, Xi C&A and DC Bridge have accumulated experience in building and operating data centers."

title: GS Retail fined 12.8 billion won over data breach affecting 1.66 million users - Korea JoongAng Daily
content: The $9.3 million penalty comes after the company failed to notify users that accounts on GS Shop and GS25 portals were compromised. GS Retail has been fined more than 12.8 billion won ($9.3 million) over a data breach that affected 1.66 million users, the Personal Information Protection Commission (PIPC) said Monday. The PIPC decided to impose a 12.84 billion won fine and a 3 million won penalty on the operator of home-shopping retailer GS Shop and convenience store chain GS25 for violating personal information protection laws at its plenary meeting on Wednesday. An unidentified hacker carried out credential-stuffing attacks on the GS Shop website from June 21, 2024, through Feb. 13, 2025, and on the GS25 website from Dec. 26, 2024, through Jan. 4, 2025. The hacker successfully accessed user accounts. Credential stuffing is a cyberattack in which hackers attempt to log in to accounts by repeatedly entering large numbers of usernames and passwords in their possession. The hacker used the compromised accounts to access pages containing members’ personal information. They reportedly extracted data from 1.58 million GS Shop users and 79,128 GS25 users. The information included name, gender, date of birth, phone number, address and email address. GS Retail did not have adequate security measures to detect and block large numbers of login attempts from the same IP address within a short period, the commission found. The company also failed to promptly recognize warning signs, including sharp increases in login attempts and failures. Lax controls allowed the data breaches to continue for an extended period, according to the PIPC. GS Retail first learned that GS25 had suffered a data breach on Jan. 4, 2025. It took the company more than a month to discover that GS Shop was being attacked in the same way. A total of 327 IP addresses used in the GS25 attack were also used to target GS Shop. The PIPC investigation also found shortcomings in GS Retail's privacy protection organization and operations. The company had no dedicated privacy protection team at the time of the breach, while its security operations were divided between separate systems. The exposure leaked the names and phone numbers of 1,140 people. title: GS Retail fined 12.8 bln won over personal data leak of 1.66 mln customers - Yonhap News Agency
content: This will let Google show Yonhap news articles that match or are related to your search SEOUL, Aug. 31 (Yonhap) -- GS Retail Co., a retail giant that operates GS25 convenience stores, has been issued a 12.8 billion-won (US$9.3 million) fine over a personal data leak that affected 1.66 million customers, the privacy watchdog said Monday. According to the Personal Information Protection Commission (PIPC), an unidentified hacker infiltrated the company's home shopping platform GS SHOP and its convenience store chain between 2024 and 2025 by repeatedly injecting a large number of pre-secured user IDs and passwords to successfully bypass login systems. Through the member information modification pages, the hacker compromised the personal data of 1.58 million GS SHOP users and 79,128 GS25 customers. The leaked information included their names, gender, dates of birth, contact numbers, home addresses and email addresses. The privacy watchdog said GS Retail failed to notice abnormal signs, such as a sharp spike in login attempts and failures from identical IP addresses within a short time frame, which allowed the unauthorized access to persist undetected over a prolonged period. The company also lacked a dedicated office for privacy protection at the time of the incident. The PIPC said it has ordered GS Retail to formulate concrete preventive measures, such as advanced security policies capable of identifying abnormal connections, and to appoint dedicated personnel for privacy protection. Song Kyung-hui, chief of the Personal Information Protection Commission, bangs the gavel during a meeting at the office of the commission in central Seoul, in this file photo taken July 29, 2026. title: GS Retail Fined 12.8 Billion Won After 1.66 Million Data Leak - Seoul Economic Daily
content:
Privacy Commission Approves Sanctions Against GS Retail
Hackers Breach GS Shop and GS25 Websites en Masse
Surge in Failed Logins Went Undetected
SK Telecom and Enlyze Also Fined South Korea's privacy regulator has imposed a fine of 12.836 billion won ($9.2 million) and an administrative penalty of 10.2 million won on GS Retail (007070) after the personal data of about 1.66 million customers was leaked. The Personal Information Protection Commission said on the 31st that it approved the measures against GS Retail for violations of personal data protection rules at a plenary meeting on the 26th. The commission also ordered the company to draw up measures to prevent a recurrence and to disclose the case on its website. The investigation found that from June 2024 to February 2025, hackers attempted to log in to member information pages on the GS Shop and GS25 websites operated by GS Retail using credential stuffing, in which previously obtained account information is entered indiscriminately. Through this method, they stole personal data including names, gender, dates of birth, contact numbers, addresses and email addresses belonging to a total of 1,660,153 people — 1,581,025 from GS Shop and 79,128 from GS25. GS Retail had no system in place to detect and block large volumes of login attempts from a single IP address over a short period, and failed to recognize the warning signs in time even as failed logins rose sharply, the commission found. The company also identified the breach at the GS25 website first in January 2025 but neglected follow-up measures, confirming the hacking of GS Shop only in February, two months after the incident. The commission ordered GS Retail to adopt a security policy capable of identifying and blocking abnormal access by analyzing service traffic volumes and patterns. It also instructed the company to assign dedicated personnel for personal data protection and to review and improve its overall governance framework, including clarifying the authority and responsibilities of its chief privacy officer. Enlyze, which operates a dating app service, was fined 118.44 million won and given an administrative penalty of 3.6 million won after personal data from 736 accounts was leaked in March 2023. The company was found to have breached its duty to take safety measures, including neglecting checks on identity verification vulnerabilities within the app and failing to block excessive access from a single IP address. A leak also occurred at A to Z, which was contracted to build and operate an event website for ifland, the metaverse platform of SK Telecom (017670). An administrator page was exposed to search engines, leaking the names and mobile phone numbers of 1,140 users from November 2022 to January 2023. According to the commission, A to Z failed to take access control measures such as IP restrictions on the administrator page, while SK Telecom reported and notified the breach late, exceeding the legally required 24 hours. The commission imposed an administrative penalty of 3.6 million won and a corrective order on SK Telecom, and issued a warning to A to Z. "When operating personal data processing systems, it is essential to comply with basic security rules such as access controls that restrict unauthorized access and periodic vulnerability checks," a commission official said. "When a leak occurs, it must be reported and notified without delay within the legal deadline so that data subjects can respond quickly." Original reporting by Lee Jin-seok for Seoul Economic Daily. title: Korea fines GS Retail over massive GS Shop, GS25 data leaks - CHOSUNBIZ - Chosunbiz
content: Watchdog slaps GS Retail with record privacy fine after missing weeks of credential-stuffing attacks The Personal Information Protection Commission imposed a 12.8 billion won penalty surcharge on GS Retail after a massive leak of customer personal information. Although red flags such as a surge in failed logins appeared, the company failed to detect and block them, and even after confirming the leak in one service, the same attack continued in another service, leading to additional leaks for about 40 days, it was found. The Personal Information Protection Commission said on the 31st that it held its 17th plenary meeting on the 26th and resolved to impose a total penalty surcharge of 12.836 billion won and fines of 3 million won on GS Retail for violating obligations on personal information protection measures. Along with corrective orders such as preparing measures to prevent recurrence, it also ordered the company to disclose the disposition on its website. The investigation found that an unidentified hacker carried out a "credential stuffing" attack by indiscriminately attempting to log in to the GS Shop and GS25 websites operated by GS Retail using IDs and passwords obtained in advance. The attacks continued from June 21, 2024, to Feb. 13, 2025, on GS Shop and from Dec. 26, 2024, to Jan. 4, 2025, on GS25. After successfully logging in, the hacker accessed pages such as the member information edit page and stole the personal information of 1,581,025 GS Shop users and 79,128 GS25 users. When a credential stuffing attack occurs, the number of login attempts and the failure rate typically spike from the same internet protocol (IP) address. However, GS Retail was found not to have prepared measures to detect and block such abnormal access. Problems also emerged in the incident response. GS Retail first identified on Jan. 4, 2025, that personal information had been leaked from the GS25 website, but it did not confirm until Feb. 13 of the same year that the same attack was underway on GS Shop. Even after recognizing the first leak, personal information continued to be leaked for about 40 days on the other service. In particular, 327 of the IP addresses used to attack GS25 were confirmed to have been used identically in the GS Shop attack. The Personal Information Protection Commission determined that at the time of the incident, GS Retail lacked a dedicated personal information protection unit and had a bifurcated security operation, indicating deficiencies in its personal information protection organization and operating system. It also found that even though 1,599 additional affected persons were identified during the investigation after the initial leak notification, the company informed them of the leak only after 72 hours had passed without justifiable reason. Accordingly, it ordered GS Retail to implement measures to prevent recurrence, such as applying security policies that analyze service traffic volume and access patterns to identify abnormal access. It also ordered comprehensive improvements to personal information protection governance, including assigning dedicated personnel for personal information protection and clarifying the authority and responsibilities of the chief privacy officer (CPO). Meanwhile, the Personal Information Protection Commission decided the same day to impose a 118.44 million won penalty surcharge and fines of 3.6 million won on dating app operator NLIZ. The investigation found that on the dating app operated by NLIZ, a hacker exploited a vulnerability in the identity verification process and, from March 23 to 27, 2023, attempted logins with 16,803 mobile phone numbers, leaking personal information such as the dates of birth, education, and occupations of 736 accounts. NLIZ was found to have neglected inspection and remediation of the app's identity verification vulnerability and failed to configure blocks even when excessive access occurred from the same IP address. In addition, SK Telecom received fines of 3.6 million won and a corrective order, while Atoz received a warning. While operating SK Telecom's "ifland" event website from Nov. 21, 2022, to Jan. 3, 2023, Atoz failed to properly control access to the administrator page, resulting in the leak of the names and mobile phone numbers of 1,140 people. The Personal Information Protection Commission said SK Telecom recognized the leak but notified and reported it past the statutory 24-hour deadline. title: GS Retail fined W12.8b over data breach affecting 1.66 million users - 헤럴드경제

GS Retail's websites — including those of GS Shop (home shopping) and GS25 (convenience store) — were subjected to hacking attacks between June 21, 2024, and Feb. 13 last year. The attacks used so-called credential stuffing, in which large volumes of previously obtained usernames and passwords are systematically tried against login systems. As a result, the personal information of about 11.58 million GS Home Shopping users and 79,128 GS25 users was exposed, including names, genders, dates of birth, contact details, addresses and email addresses. GS Retail had failed to put in place measures to detect and block mass login attempts originating from the same internet protocol address. Even as abnormal spikes in login attempts and failures emerged as warning signs, the company did not recognize them, allowing the breach to continue for an extended period. The company first detected the GS25 website breach on Jan. 4 last year but was slow to respond. It did not discover until February last year that the same type of attack was simultaneously targeting the GS Home Shopping website. As a result, personal data continued to leak from Jan. 4 through Feb. 13 of that year, even after the initial breach was identified. Investigators also found that 327 of the IP addresses used in the GS25 attack were the same ones used against GS Shop. The commission also found that GS Retail lacked a dedicated personal data protection unit at the time of the incident and operated a fragmented security structure. During the investigation following the initial breach notification, an additional 1,599 affected individuals were identified, but the company notified them more than 72 hours after discovery without justifiable cause. The commission ordered GS Retail to publish the details of the sanctions on its website, establish and implement recurrence-prevention measures — including security policies capable of identifying abnormal access — and assign dedicated personal data protection staff while clarifying the authority and responsibilities of its chief privacy officer. Meanwhile, the commission fined Enlaiz, the operator of a dating app, 118.44 million won and imposed an administrative penalty of 3.6 million won over the leak of personal data from 736 accounts. SK Telecom was also sanctioned with an administrative penalty of 3.6 million won. Atoz, which was commissioned by SK Telecom to run events for its "ifland" service and built and operated an event website for that purpose, leaked the names and mobile phone numbers of 1,140 people after failing to restrict access to its administrator page by IP address. SK Telecom received its administrative penalty for reporting the data breach more than 24 hours after it occurred.

title: Personal Information Protection Commission Fines GS Retail 12.8 Billion Won for Breach Affecting 1.58 Million Members - 아시아경제
content:
Personal Information Protection Commission Fines GS Retail 12.8 Billion Won for Breach Affecting 1.58 Million Members GS Retail, which failed to prevent the personal data breach involving approximately 1.58 million members, has been fined around 12.8 billion won. The Personal Information Protection Commission announced on August 31 that it held its 17th general meeting on August 26 and imposed an administrative fine of 12,836 million won and an additional penalty of 3 million won on GS Retail for violating personal information protection regulations. The commission also decided to issue a corrective order to establish measures to prevent recurrence, and mandated that the incident results be published on the company's website. According to the commission's investigation, a hacker succeeded in logging into some member accounts by carrying out a ‘credential stuffing’ attack on the websites operated by GS Retail—namely, the GSSHOP home shopping site and the GS25 convenience store site. Credential stuffing is a type of cyberattack in which attackers use previously acquired username and password combinations to attempt logins en masse; this typically causes a sharp increase in both login attempts and failure rates. The hacker then accessed the member information modification pages, resulting in the exposure of personal data for 1,581,025 people from GSSHOP and 79,128 people from GS25. The leaked personal information included names, gender, date of birth, contact information, addresses, and email addresses. The investigation found that GS Retail did not have measures in place to detect or block mass login attempts from the same IP address in a short period of time. Consequently, the company failed to recognize the abnormal surge in login attempts and failures, resulting in the continued exposure of personal data. GS Retail first became aware of the breach on the GS25 website on January 4 last year but did not learn that the same attack was occurring on the GSSHOP website until the following February. Additionally, at the time of the incident, there was no dedicated department responsible for personal information protection, and the security operations were divided, reflecting deficiencies in both the structure and management of personal information protection. Furthermore, 1,599 additional affected users were identified during the investigation after the initial breach notification, but it was confirmed that notification of this data breach was delayed beyond 72 hours without legitimate reason. The Personal Information Protection Commission ordered the company to implement security policies capable of identifying abnormal access as part of its measures to prevent similar incidents from recurring. The commission also issued a corrective order to strengthen governance, instructing GS Retail to assign dedicated personnel for personal information protection, ensure rapid incident response, and review and improve the authority and responsibility of the Chief Privacy Officer (CPO). Enrise, which operates the dating app service ‘Wippy,’ was fined 118.44 million won and received an additional penalty of 3.6 million won. The hacker exploited a vulnerability in the identity verification process of the dating app service, attempted to log in using 16,803 phone numbers, and leaked the personal information of 736 accounts. Leaked information included nickname, gender, profile photo, date of birth, personality traits, education, occupation, height, and blood type. The investigation found that Enrise both neglected to address and review vulnerabilities in the app's identity verification and failed to establish a policy to block excessive access attempts from the same IP address. SK Telecom was issued a penalty of 3.6 million won and a corrective order, while Atoz received a warning. Atoz, which was contracted by SKT to operate an event-specific website for the 'Ifland' service, exposed the administrator page to search engines, resulting in the disclosure of personal information (names and mobile phone numbers) of 1,140 people. Atoz failed to implement access controls, such as restricting administrator page access by IP address. In addition, SKT reported and notified of the personal data breach only after more than 24 hours had passed. The commission emphasized, "When operating personal information processing systems, it is essential to implement access controls to restrict unauthorized access, and to conduct periodic vulnerability checks and corrective actions as basic principles." The commission added, "In the event of a personal data breach, both notification and reporting must be completed within 72 hours to enable information subjects to quickly recognize and respond to the incident." © The Asia Business Daily.
